correctness.rationale: Classify all line-graph cliques as vertex stars or edge-triangles. Under minimum source degree three, each star is a facet, two stars meet in at most one edge-vertex, and a central triangle has at most two vertices from any star. After stellar subdivision, every higher proper star face is free with its barycenter cone in descending size; every nontriangle star-pair is then free. The residual faces equal the canonical midpoint subdivision exactly, and pair stabilizers match. For complete graphs, contraction with coordinate sum gives ker partial_2 = exterior cube of the integral augmentation lattice; the 2-skeleton is simply connected. Literal finite free-face and group-matrix checks reproduced all specified examples, but the general mathematical proof does not rely on finite tests.

originality.rationale: Prior work covers the nonequivariant wedge (2004), the ordinary line-graph homotopy equivalence (2020), and the all-k rational character in principle (2026 online). The submitted result instead provides an explicit automorphism-equivariant orbitwise simplicial collapse for every finite simple graph with minimum degree at least three and an integral homology lattice for the complete-graph family. Specific full-text checks and statement-implication comparisons did not identify an earlier construction of the stronger result; publication priority remains nondefinitive.
residual_risks: A stronger unindexed equivariant nerve or simple-homotopy theorem could imply the constructive equivariant result.
The rational character and the ordinary wedge and two-skeleton homotopy are already covered; originality rests on the explicit orbitwise collapse and the integral lattice.
No independent expert or exhaustive publication-priority review is claimed; one plausible 2008 publisher text was only partly accessible.

value.rationale: The graph-uniform, automorphism-equivariant simple-collapse construction is stronger than ordinary homotopy type and allows all subgroup fixed-point and quotient calculations. The complete-graph specialization identifies a precise integral S_n-lattice relevant to the explicitly raised bounded-matching representation question; neither Betti ranks nor rational characters alone distinguish integral lattice structures. The output is a structural reusable method, not a parameter slice or a routine rank recomputation.
